claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature-processed single-phase ZrB2 has inadequate oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
Combining ZrB2 with HfB2, TaB2, NbB2, and TiB2 can produce a single-phase high-entropy diboride.
High-entropy diborides can be fabricated using high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
The proposed high-entropy diboride can be synthesized below 1700 °C.
The intervention produces a disordered, homogeneous high-entropy diboride phase.
Multi-element interactions in the high-entropy phase lower sintering activation barriers.
The high-entropy effect stabilizes the diboride phase at reduced processing temperatures.
The diverse refractory elements promote formation of protective oxide layers.
The high-entropy composition reduces diffusion rates of aggressive species.
Reduced diffusion of aggressive species improves liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
The proposed high-entropy diboride will achieve adequate densification and structural integrity when sintered below 1700 °C.
The proposed high-entropy diboride will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed high-entropy diboride will have better liquid-metal corrosion resistance than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Prior lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens exhibit poorer oxidation and corrosion performance.
The proposed improvements are expected to persist during oxidizing service at temperatures up to approximately 1500 °C.
The proposed improvements require compositions that retain a single-phase high-entropy structure.
